prompt:
Implement A10 revocation, expiry and local privacy retirement in this isolated native osstack worktree. Actual parent Claude Fable 5.1 will challenge the exact final candidate. No Claude calls yourself, no subagents, commits, push, deploy or real messages. Only modify the 8 briefs modules listed below and create tests/test_brief_revocation.py and tests/test_brief_retention.py; preserve all old tests, dependencies, docs and queue. Allowed existing modules: store.py, service.py, worker.py, delivery.py, card_delivery.py, callbacks.py, revisions.py. New retention.py. You may leave unnecessary existing files unchanged. Read README/architecture/deployment and relevant contracts/tests. Native parent captures full allowed-file snapshots regardless of which changed.

A10 AC: while generating, revoke blocks subsequent provider egress/delivery and stale fence publication; expired raw/excerpts are cleaned with permanent tombstones preventing cache/index resurrection; already sent remote cards cannot be guaranteed recalled, hash-only evidence must never present as currently re-verifiable. Scope: implement a real opt-in local retention/revocation domain coordinator plus explicit hooks into existing services/ledgers, with actual SQL cleanup of current local payload-bearing records. A11 owns scheduler/global server composition. Do NOT settle for a standalone unused tombstone class or a doc-only plan. Do not invent remote deletion/cryptographic filesystem erasure claims.

Architecture constraints (choose a compact concrete design, explain choices in source docstrings):
1. Separate explicitly initialized owned RetentionLedger with strict application_id/version/exact DDL, bounded record counts, canonical metadata only (no source excerpts/drafts/correction bodies/capabilities), fixed sanitized errors/repr, integer/UTC clock validation, monotonic highwater and immutable expiry. Use DELETE/EXTRA for new durable authority, bounded SQLite busy handling. A retention decision is NOT user-authenticated by request flags: expose trusted RequesterContext scoped operations; injected local maintenance/admin authority must authorize source/grant revocation or clearing another scope. Deny unrelated actor/namespace. A source revoke must be stable against changing source_id, job_id or delivery_id in caches: scope plus trusted resource/grant/snapshot identity needs an explicit stable key. Distinguish permanent resource revocation versus expiry of a pinned snapshot and document whether newer snapshots can ever be admitted; no reset/reopen API. Store no raw sources in tombstone metadata. Hashes are integrity hints, never authority or source re-verification.
2. Track jobs from actual authoritative BriefStore row + frozen source snapshots, NOT caller-provided arbitrary payload/path/manifest. Bind exact namespace/principal/job/original source identities, revision and known ledger targets; no arbitrary file paths from external requests. Supplied expiry/policy comes only from trusted composition and cannot extend existing expiry on replay (even after restart); operations at == expires must deny, without waiting for sweeper. Define untracked jobs fail-closed when retention is enabled; do not silently treat missing registration as authorization. A11 must register/dispatch in the documented order if full automatic admission isn't safely atomic yet. Old unconfigured features stay compatible, but explicit retention-enabled services cannot silently skip a missing/failed gate.
3. Durable tombstone FIRST, then scoped primary cancellation/fence invalidation and retryable per-ledger cleanup, never the reverse. Multiple databases cannot have one atomic transaction: persisted cleanup progress and idempotent resume after every boundary, no active authority restored by partial failure. Never mark cleanup complete until required targets are actually verified retired; missing/unavailable/foreign ledger is pending failure, not success. Do not retain arbitrary callbacks serialized into manifests. Known configured stores must be explicit owned instances with stable target identity on reopen; swapping/omitting one cannot falsely mark complete. A local service cancellation signal should stop active acceptance before waiting for SQL; primary durable cancellation/fence is authoritative across restart. Concurrent cleaners/registrations and lost commit acknowledgements must not erase newer/unrelated jobs or misstate success. Tombstones stay indefinitely unless a future deliberate migration specifies otherwise; capacity exhaustion cannot silently delete/recycle them. Permanent source/snapshot tombstones must block fresh intake from stale cache too, not just old job replay.
4. Integrate explicit opt-in current retention checks into BriefService generation gates and original stored preview/callback/TEXT/Card/Revision services (or a clearly mandatory typed composed guard actually exercised by their real paths). Check AFTER awaited connection/DB/render waits at actual egress and private result release, including count/create, TEXT read/send, card create ACK acceptance, callbacks, correction/adoption. Existing trusted current authorizers still must check all original source/grant/private-binding permissions. Retention is additional authority, never a substitute. Preserve original current-clock/deadline checks after all waits. Primary SQL must precede final authority checks; if retention uses its own bounded read at the authorization point, avoid lock-order cycles: never hold the retention transaction while acquiring other ledger locks, fail closed on unavailable authority, and document this narrow local-I/O contract instead of pretending all callbacks do no IO. Do not rely on a stale process-local cache alone across instances/restart. Strictly recheck that guards are configured/typed/callable as required; never trust a client boolean. Local authorization point cannot revoke bytes already handed off to remote systems: preserve this boundary accurately.
5. Implement scoped sanctioned retirement helpers on each owned store, retaining permanent identity/idempotency/send/lease/cost tombstones while removing payloads from ALL relevant local content copies: BriefStore job payload (source excerpts/goals/config), original revision payload/provenance; U01 frozen intent wire, full observations/receipts that include content; card preview/card/wire/response_card plus live callback capabilities; A06 root snapshot and correction event text/history; legacy callback capabilities. Preserve unknown/started spend and original send custody rather than refund/retry or reset to pending. Check cost profile/config may contain prompt_template: do not leave raw prompt text under the guise of cost metadata; preserve just sufficient immutable numeric accounting/digests and post-retirement settlement semantics. Audit all tables for content, not only obvious source_excerpt names. Prefer compatible additive owned schema/tombstone state or clearly validated retired sentinel state; never casually corrupt canonical rows and then call that a coherent status. Redacted APIs should return an explicit safe retired/hash-only status or deny reads, NOT deserialize removed content as an active fresh draft/intent or accept old copies to refill it. Old binaries/reopened old configured objects must not reopen a send; keep permanent job/card rows where needed. Do not delete whole files or run unrelated table wipes. Validate exact ownership/schema before modification, reject foreign/future without mutation. secure_delete=ON on cleanup connection is useful for current ordinary SQLite pages; verify logical SQL absence and synthetic raw-byte sentinel absence in owned live DB where feasible, but do NOT promise erasure of backups/WAL external files/SSD snapshots/process memory/remote cards. Existing in-flight RAM snapshots must fail gates and late ACK/LLM replies must never repopulate erased bodies.
6. Privacy-preserving retention status: distinguish authorized/expired/revoked, cleanup pending/partial/complete and irrecoverable uncertainty as appropriate; no requester leaks from cross-scope lookups. Return only bounded non-sensitive reason codes/counts/IDs; cleaned records cannot display content_verified/reverifiable/human_received true simply because old digests survive. Preserve historical send facts separately from current content availability, and explicitly say remotely sent cards may persist. No remote recall network calls. Repeated cleanup and source-revoke operations stable idempotency; changed same-key input conflicts. No arbitrary user text in errors, exception contexts, logs or repr.

Verification: RED before GREEN meaningful tests. Use /Volumes/AIMATE_WORK/Developer/CodeX/OStag-company-integration/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_brief_revocation.py tests/test_brief_retention.py, then Ruff. Parent full suite baseline2498 plus 14 old independent gates; DO NOT run full old suite in nested sandbox or weaken/modify old tests. Tests must exercise real existing A04 worker/provider guards (pause between count and create / awaited egress / after response before complete), U01 and card services, signed callback domain path, A06 correction/adoption. Revoke/expire during active generation, late result cannot complete/store/publish; direct durable fence check fails and later send denied; cancelled unknown costs stay conservative. Build actual generation/outbox, TEXT observed data, acknowledged card/navigation, legacy callback and correction history with synthetic private marker, retire and reopen all databases, assert current live SQL/owned file content absence, no source-cache/new-event resurrection, original message/card identity cannot get another send. Test missing/unavailable target, crash after each cleanup stage and before progress receipt, changed target identity/reopen, a second unrelated user's data untouched, cross-scope maintenance denied, foreign/future schema unchanged, expiry at boundary/time rollback, repeated registration cannot renew expiry, multi-connection races, shared authority missing/busy denies, cleanup capacities and malformed policy types. Include real deterministic barriers for waited-lock/async scenarios; do not label a pre-lock race as actual lock wait. Avoid gratuitous schema migrations; if changing schema compatibility, preserve baseline fixtures/parent gates and explicit opt-in upgrades. No live destructive cleanup: only synthetic test stores.

No default scheduler or server settings wiring in this slice; document exactly how trusted callers register a stored job, enable gates, revoke/expire and run/resume cleanup. Actual A11 composition remains future, but callable lifecycle and guards must work end-to-end locally now. All old store schemas and API semantics stay compatible when A10 is not enabled. Return concise actual results and remaining integration constraints. Parent updates MD and performs real Fable review.
